title: Yogyakarta vs Solo: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Yogyakarta for first-timers, temples, and the classic Java experience. Solo for authentic local life, batik, and better street food. Both cities are 1 hour apart by cheap train — do both.

categories.name: Temples & Heritage
categories.summary: Borobudur and Prambanan are world-class UNESCO sites. Solo has the underrated Cetho and Sukuh on Mount Lawu.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: Solo's nasi liwet, soto Solo, and timlo are rated higher than Yogyakarta's gudeg by most travelers.

categories.name: Daily Budget
categories.summary: Solo is cheaper across the board — guesthouses Rp 70k-150k vs Yogya's Rp 100k-200k.

categories.name: Tourist Infrastructure
categories.summary: Yogyakarta has a full backpacker circuit, English menus, and organized tours. Solo is more local-facing.

categories.name: Authenticity
categories.summary: Reddit consistently describes Solo as 'what Yogyakarta used to be like 20 years ago.'

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Borobudur, Prambanan, and Merapi jeep tours make Yogyakarta the undisputed day-trip hub.

categories.name: Batik Shopping
categories.summary: Pasar Klewer is Indonesia's batik capital. Yogyakarta's Malioboro batik is tourist-grade by comparison.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: Yogyakarta has craft beer bars and live music on Prawirotaman. Solo is quiet after dark.

faq.question: Is Yogyakarta or Solo better for a first-time visitor to Java?
faq.answer: Yogyakarta is the better base for first-timers.

faq.question: How far is Yogyakarta from Solo and how do I get there?
faq.answer: 65km apart, ~1 hour by KAI commuter train for Rp 8,000-15,000 ($0.50-1).

faq.question: What is Solo (Surakarta) known for?
faq.answer: Solo is famous as Indonesia's batik capital (Pasar Klewer), authentic Javanese royal court culture, and exceptional local cuisine including nasi liwet, soto Solo, and timlo.
